subject: MSA + Private Deployment Annex — sovereign backup & validation carveout
messages:
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@valleyhealth.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-22T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: MSA + Private Deployment Annex — sovereign backup & validation carveout

Hi Laura,

Thanks for the demo last week. As we move toward procurement, Legal and InfoSec have a few specific asks we need to resolve in the MSA + Private Deployment annex before we can sign the Order Form:

1) Sovereign backup carveout — ValleyHealth requires an option to deposit a sealed snapshot with an independent custodian for disaster recovery; the snapshot must be cryptographically sealed and access-controlled.
2) Third-party validation — our auditors want a defined scope: either an onsite witness certification of a snapshot deposit or a remote attestation with vendor-provided artifacts.
3) License/residency boundary — clarify that runtime residency is limited to the customer VPC region and that Redwood has no rights to derive or sell customer-trained models.

Can you share a redline of the annex and an evidence matrix showing what artifacts we can provide for each validation option? We are aiming to finish review by end of week so procurement can issue a PO.

Attachments: none on our side yet — I can share ValleyHealth’s standard MSA template if helpful.

Regards,
Daniel Park
Director, Information Security
ValleyHealth Systems

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@valleyhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-22T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA + Private Deployment Annex — sovereign backup & validation carveout

Daniel — thanks for the clear list. We can support both options (witness certification or remote attestation) but the mechanisms and commercial carveouts differ, so we'll propose two paths in the annex.

Plan: I’ll send an annotated redline of the Private Deployment annex plus an evidence matrix that maps each validation option to artifacts (sealed snapshot checksum + witness logs, archived KV-cache dumps, transient operator access logs, signed attestation report). I’ve attached the draft redlines and matrix for your review.

A couple of clarifying Qs that will affect language and pricing:
- For the sealed snapshot, do you require an on-site witness from ValleyHealth/legal or is a third-party custodian + vendor witness sufficient?
- For the license boundary, is ValleyHealth asking for an explicit “no-derivative-works” covenant or a scoped-use limitation on our side?

We can propose contract text for both approaches; if we can get your preference on the above by EOD tomorrow we’ll lock the language and route to Marcus (legal) for final redlines.

Attachment: Redwood_MSA_Annex_v3_redlines.docx (annotated redline)
Attachment: evidence_matrix.xlsx (artifact mapping)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-22T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA + Private Deployment Annex — sovereign backup & validation carveout (internal)

Team — looping in Marcus to drive legal language. Quick notes after reviewing Laura's draft: 

1) License/residency: propose this clause — "Customer Data and Customer-Trained Models remain the exclusive property of Customer; Redwood shall not sell, license, or otherwise commercialize derivatives of Customer Data or Customer-Trained Models. Runtime residency for Private Deployment will be bounded to the Customer VPC region(s) listed in the Order Form." This is tighter than our standard but aligns with enterprise asks. Marcus, can you confirm we can accept this with a limited carveout for debugging telemetry?

2) Sealed snapshot options: offer two alternatives in Annex A: (A) Sealed-snapshot deposit to an independent custodian with Redwood-signed witness log (suitable for DR-only); (B) Sealed-snapshot + onsite witness certification (ValleyHealth representative + third-party custodian) which carries a one-time setup fee. We should include acceptance criteria for checksum verification and a window for witness scheduling (30 days).

3) Third-party validation artifacts: evidence_matrix.xlsx maps artifacts to validation levels. We should ensure the attestation report includes a signed statement of environment hash, operator identity (SAML/SSH audit), and a time-windowed KV cache capture. Remote attestations will be allowed for lower-sensitivity datasets.

Action items: Marcus to draft final redline language for the two snapshot options and the "no-derivative" clause; Marcus + Connor to confirm expected delivery timeline for evidence artifacts; Laura to propose commercial for option B (one-time witness/setup fee). Aim to have final redlines by COB tomorrow so Laura can send to ValleyHealth.

Karthik
Director, Solutions (Redwood Inference)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@valleyhealth.com>, ValleyHealth Legal <legal@valleyhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-23T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA + Private Deployment Annex — sovereign backup & validation carveout

Daniel / ValleyHealth Legal — attaching the redline and evidence matrix per our notes. Thanks to Karthik and Marcus for the rapid turnaround.

Summary of what we propose (high level):
- License boundary: explicit "no-derivative-works" covenant plus a scoped operational telemetry carveout (telemetry will be anonymized and used only for reliability/bugfixing; no model training).
- Snapshot validation: two selectable options in Annex A —
  Option 1: Custodian deposit + Redwood-signed witness logs. No onsite cost.
  Option 2: Custodian deposit + onsite witness certification (ValleyHealth or third-party witness) — includes one-time setup & scheduling fee (est. $12,000).
- Evidence artifacts: the attached evidence_matrix.xlsx shows the minimal deliverables for each option (checksum + signed witness log; KV-cache digest; operator access logs; attestation report). Remote attestation acceptable for lower-sensitivity workloads; onsite witness required when PHI-level data is in-scope.

Next steps: please confirm which snapshot validation option ValleyHealth prefers and whether you require a ValleyHealth representative onsite for the witness. If you agree, we’ll prepare final Order Form language and a short SOW for the witness setup (for Option 2).

Attachments: Redwood_MSA_Annex_v3_redlines.docx; evidence_matrix.xlsx
